24303-the-philadelphia-magazines-and-the.creator: Unknown
24303-the-philadelphia-magazines-and-the.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. I have done my best to make the story, dull and dreary as it surely is at times, not unworthy of its subject, or of the city that it describes, and of which I grow fonder year by year.

29305-sielanka-an-idyll.title: _An Idyll_
29305-sielanka-an-idyll.creator: Unknown
29305-sielanka-an-idyll.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. swayed in the wind, and with every breeze its leaves touched the dilapidated moss-covered straw thatch of the roof; when the stronger gusts of wind bent its boughs to the wall, and pressed its twigs and the waves of leaves against the roof, it would seem as if the tree loved the house and embraced it.

arxiv-2104-10603.title: GAN-Based Data Augmentation and Anonymization for Skin-Lesion Analysis: A Critical Review
arxiv-2104-10603.creator: Alceu Bissoto 1 Eduardo Valle 2 Sandra Avila 1 1 Institute of Computing (IC) 2 School of Electrical and Computing Engineering (FEEC) RECOD Lab, University of Campinas (UNICAMP), Brazil
arxiv-2104-10603.description: Abstract Despite the growing availability of high-quality public datasets, the lack of training samples is still one of the main challenges of deep-learning for skin lesion analysis. Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) appear as an enticing alternative to alleviate the issue, by synthesizing samples indistinguishable from real images, with a plethora of works employing them for medical applications.

arxiv-2106-07656.title: The M-dwarf Ultraviolet Spectroscopic Sample I. Determining Stellar Parameters for Field Stars
arxiv-2106-07656.creator: J. Sebastian Pineda, Allison Youngblood, Kevin France
arxiv-2106-07656.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by J. Sebastian Pineda, Allison Youngblood, Kevin France. Accurate stellar properties are essential for precise stellar astrophysics and exoplanetary science. In the M-dwarf regime, much effort has gone into defining empirical relations that can use readily accessible observables to assess physical stellar properties. Often, these relations for the quantity of interest are cast as a non-linear function of available data; however, in Bayesian modeling the reverse is needed.

arxiv-2210-03571.title: Bayesian Calibration of the Intelligent Driver Model
arxiv-2210-03571.creator: Chengyuan Zhang, and Lijun Sun
arxiv-2210-03571.description: Abstract Accurate calibration of car-following models is essential for understanding human driving behaviors and implementing high-fidelity microscopic simulations. This work proposes a memory-augmented Bayesian calibration technique to capture both uncertainty in the model parameters and the temporally correlated behavior discrepancy between model predictions and observed data.

arxiv-2301-01974.title: The Generalised (Uniform) Mazur Intersection Property
arxiv-2301-01974.creator: Pradipta Bandyopadhyay, Deepak Gothwal
arxiv-2301-01974.description: Abstract . Given a family 𝒞 \mathcal{C} of closed bounded convex sets in a Banach space X X , we say that X X has the 𝒞 \mathcal{C} -MIP if every C ∈ 𝒞 C\in\mathcal{C} is the intersection of the closed balls containing it.

arxiv-2305-09376.title: Configuration mixing and intertwined quantum phase transitions in odd-mass niobium isotopes
arxiv-2305-09376.creator: N. Gavrielov
arxiv-2305-09376.description: Abstract Nuclei in the Z ≈ 40 , N ≈ 60 Z\!\approx\!40,N\!\approx\!60 region have one of the most complicated structural evolution across the nuclear chart, with coexisting shapes arising from different mixed configurations. In such a region, it is difficult to investigate odd-mass nuclei. In this paper a new algebraic framework is introduced, the interacting boson-fermion model with configuration mixing.

arxiv-2309-16592.title: Tensor Factorization for Leveraging Cross-Modal Knowledge in Data-Constrained Infrared Object Detection
arxiv-2309-16592.creator: Manish Sharma, Moitreya Chatterjee, Kuan-Chuan Peng, Suhas Lohit, Michael Jones
arxiv-2309-16592.description: Abstract While state-of-the-art object detection methods have reached some level of maturity for regular RGB images, there is still some distance to be covered before these methods perform comparably on Infrared (IR) images. The primary bottleneck towards accomplishing this goal is the lack of sufficient labeled training data in the IR modality, owing to the cost of acquiring such data.

arxiv-2312-04982.title: Boosting Prompt-Based Self-Training With Mapping-Free Automatic Verbalizer for Multi-Class Classification
arxiv-2312-04982.creator: Yookyung Kho, Jaehee Kim, Pilsung Kang
arxiv-2312-04982.description: Abstract Recently, prompt-based fine-tuning has garnered considerable interest as a core technique for few-shot text classification task. This approach reformulates the fine-tuning objective to align with the Masked Language Modeling (MLM) objective. Leveraging unlabeled data, prompt-based self-training has shown greater effectiveness in binary and three-class classification.

arxiv-2407-03829.title: Recovering Initial States in Semilinear Parabolic Problems from Time-Averages
arxiv-2407-03829.creator: Lina Sophie Schmitz, Christoph Walker
arxiv-2407-03829.description: Abstract . Well-posedness of certain semilinear parabolic problems with nonlocal initial conditions is shown in time-weighted spaces. The result is applied to recover the initial states in semilinear parabolic problems with nonlinearities of superlinear behavior near zero from small time-averages over arbitrary time periods. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification 35K58,35Q99 1.

arxiv-2407-21498.title: MaskUno: Switch-Split Block For Enhancing Instance Segmentation
arxiv-2407-21498.creator: Jawad Haidar, Marc Mouawad, Imad Elhajj, Daniel Asmar
arxiv-2407-21498.description: Abstract Instance segmentation is an advanced form of image segmentation which, beyond traditional segmentation, requires identifying individual instances of repeating objects in a scene. Mask R-CNN is the most common architecture for instance segmentation, and improvements to this architecture include steps such as benefiting from bounding box refinements, adding semantics, or backbone enhancements.

arxiv-2412-15983.title: Never Reset Again: A Mathematical Framework for Continual Inference in Recurrent Neural Networks Thanks: The authors gratefully acknowledge the helpful discussions with Sander Bohte and Simeon Kanya. This work has been funded by the Dutch Organization for Scientific Research (NWO) with Grant KICH1.S
arxiv-2412-15983.creator: Bojian Yin, Federico Corradi
arxiv-2412-15983.description: Abstract Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) are widely used for sequential processing but face fundamental limitations with continual inference due to state saturation, requiring disruptive hidden state resets. However, reset-based methods impose synchronization requirements with input boundaries and increase computational costs at inference.

arxiv-2502-03515.title: The Emperor’s New Arc: gigaparsec patterns abound in a Λ \Lambda CDM universe 2022 The Emperor’s New Arc: gigaparsec patterns abound in a Λ \Lambda CDM universe – References
arxiv-2502-03515.creator: Till Sawala, Meri Teeriaho, Carlos S. Frenk, John Helly, Adrian Jenkins, Gabor Racz, Matthieu Schaller, Joop Schaye
arxiv-2502-03515.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Till Sawala, Meri Teeriaho, Carlos S. Frenk, John Helly, Adrian Jenkins, Gabor Racz, Matthieu Schaller, Joop Schaye. Recent discoveries of apparent large-scale features in the structure of the universe extending over many hundreds of megaparsecs, have been claimed to contradict the large-scale isotropy and homogeneity foundational to the standard ( Λ \Lambda CDM) cosmological model. We explicitly test and refute this conjecture using FLAMINGO-10K , a new and very large cosmological simulation of the growth of structure in a Λ \Lambda CDM context.

arxiv-2508-14540.title: Post-hoc LLM-Supported Debugging of Distributed Processes
arxiv-2508-14540.creator: Dennis Schiese, Andreas Both
arxiv-2508-14540.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Dennis Schiese, Andreas Both. In this paper, we address the problem of manual debugging, which nowadays remains resource-intensive and in some parts archaic. This problem is especially evident in increasingly complex and distributed software systems. Therefore, our objective of this work is to introduce an approach that can possibly be applied to any system, at both the macro- and micro-level, to ease this debugging process. This approach utilizes a system’s process data, in conjunction with generative AI, to generate natural-language explanations.

arxiv-2511-10072.title: Tree-Based Stochastic Optimization for Solving Large-Scale Urban Network Security Games
arxiv-2511-10072.creator: Shuxin Zhuang, Linjian Meng, Shuxin Li, Minming Li, Youzhi Zhang
arxiv-2511-10072.description: Abstract Urban Network Security Games (UNSGs), which model the strategic allocation of limited security resources on city road networks, are critical for urban safety. However, finding a Nash Equilibrium (NE) in large-scale UNSGs is challenging due to their massive and combinatorial action spaces.

arxiv-2602-08733.title: Foundation Inference Models for Ordinary Differential Equations
arxiv-2602-08733.creator: Maximilian Mauel, Johannes R. Hübers, David Berghaus, Patrick Seifner, Ramsés J. Sánchez
arxiv-2602-08733.description: Abstract Ordinary differential equations (ODEs) are central to scientific modelling, but inferring their vector fields from noisy trajectories remains challenging. Current approaches such as symbolic regression, Gaussian process (GP) regression, and Neural ODEs often require complex training pipelines and substantial machine learning expertise, or they depend strongly on system-specific prior knowledge.

arxiv-2603-04989.title: TAPFormer: Robust Arbitrary Point Tracking via Transient Asynchronous Fusion of Frames and Events
arxiv-2603-04989.creator: Jiaxiong Liu, Zhen Tan, Jinpu Zhang, Yi Zhou, Hui Shen, Xieyuanli Chen Dewen Hu

europmc-pmc8382161.title: Genome-wide gene expression tuning reveals diverse vulnerabilities of M. tuberculosis.
europmc-pmc8382161.creator: Bosch B, DeJesus MA, Poulton NC, Poulton NC, Zhang W, Engelhart CA, Zaveri A, Lavalette S, Ruecker N, Trujillo C, Wallach JB, Li S, Ehrt S, Chait BT, Schnappinger D, Rock JM.
europmc-pmc8382161.description: Antibacterial agents target the products of essential genes but rarely achieve complete target inhibition. Thus, the all-or-none definition of essentiality afforded by traditional genetic approaches fails to discern the most attractive bacterial targets: those whose incomplete...

pmc-10552333.title: Untangling Tetanus: A Comprehensive Case Report Describing Its Diagnosis and Treatment
pmc-10552333.creator: Özgür Söğüt, Hüseyin Ergenc, Yavuz Yigit
pmc-10552333.description: Tetanus, caused by a grave and potentially lethal bacteria, is a medical condition that severely affects the central nervous system and demands vigilant attention and comprehensive preventive measures to safeguard public health. The onset of this condition is sudden and characterized by the emergence of intense tonic muscle spasms, underscoring its critical nature.

pmc-10597525.title: Using decoys and camera traps to estimate depredation rates and neonate survival
pmc-10597525.creator: Hailey M. Boone, Krishna Pacifici, Christopher E. Moorman, Roland Kays, Paulo Corti, Paulo Corti, Paulo Corti
pmc-10597525.description: Ungulate neonates—individuals less than four weeks old—typically experience the greatest predation rates, and variation in their survival can influence ungulate population dynamics. Typical methods to measure neonate survival involve capture and radio-tracking of adults and neonates to discover mortality events.

pmc-10631155.title: Pilot study: is there an influence of lower limb positioning during magnetic resonance imaging on muscle cross section shape assessment in the thigh?
pmc-10631155.creator: Katja Oberhofer, Matthias Blum, Basil Achermann, Silvio R. Lorenzetti
pmc-10631155.description: Positioning in an MRI can influence quantitative measures of the muscle. The goal of this pilot study was to assess the influence of different levels of knee elevation during MRI on the predicted cross-sectional muscle shape in the thigh. Data were acquired in three healthy male participants (age: 29.3 ± 5.1y, height: 181.3 ± 6.4cm, weight: 85.1 ± 3.7kg).

pmc-10822926.title: Dynamic changes in the migratory microbial components of colon tissue during different periods of sepsis in an LPS-induced rat model
pmc-10822926.creator: Hao Xu, Jia You, Wenqin He, Lingpeng Pei, Yue Han, Xueer Wang, Zhigang Tian, Xiwei Zheng, Enqi Wu, Yaqin Ling
pmc-10822926.description: Previous studies have shown that bacterial translocation may play an important role in worsening gastrointestinal injury during sepsis. However, the dynamics of specific microbiota components in intestinal tissues at different sepsis stages remain unclear. Rats receiving intraperitoneal lipopolysaccharide (LPS) were sacrificed at 12 h and 48 h post-injection.

pmc-11424110.title: Assessment of Five-Year Relative Survival of Patients With Endometrial Cancer: A Period Analysis
pmc-11424110.creator: Xiao Jiao Zhao, Xin Bing, Qi Qi Lei, Yong Ran Cheng, Jun Yang, Liang You Wang, Tian Hua Chen, Tian Hui Chen
pmc-11424110.description: BackgroundEndometrial cancer is one of the most common female cancers globally and in China. Although timely assessment of 5-year relative survival is crucial for guiding secondary prevention and early screening programs for endometrial cancer patients, those kinds of data are scarce in China.

pmc-11532837.title: Binocular imbalance measured by SSVEP predicts impaired stereoacuity in amblyopia
pmc-11532837.creator: Jingyi Hu, Jing Chen, Minbin Yu, Yixuan Ku
pmc-11532837.description: PurposeThe current study aims to implement steady-state visual evoked potentials (SSVEPs) in quantifying the binocular imbalance of amblyopia and to assess the predictive value of SSVEP-derived indices for amblyopic stereoacuity.MethodsWe measure frequency-tagged SSVEP responses elicited by each eye (F1 = 6 Hz through the fellow eye; F2 = 7.

pmc-11935490.title: Higher soluble thrombomodulin and angiogenic markers in continuous flow left ventricular assist device–supported patients associated with arteriovenous malformation and nonsurgical bleeding
pmc-11935490.creator: Kavitha Muthiah, Louise L. Dunn, Hunter Eckford, David Connor, Desiree Robson, Peter S. Macdonald, Christopher S. Hayward
pmc-11935490.description: Bleeding complications are a bane of continuous flow left ventricular assist devices (cfLVAD); gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) from arteriovenous malformation (AVM) predominating. We hypothesized that shear stress disrupts vascular endothelium altering angiogenesis and contributing to bleeding. We profiled markers of endothelial dysfunction (soluble thrombomodulin [sTM]) and angiogenesis (angiopoietin-1 [Ang-1], angiopoietin-2 [Ang-2]) in 21 patients implanted with a centrifugal cfLVAD.

pmc-12579448.title: Hemosuccus Pancreaticus in a 50-Year-Old Male with Chronic Pancreatitis. A Case Report
pmc-12579448.creator: Georgina Lasoi, Faith Ameda, Rita Nassanga, Edrine Mulema, Innocent Luwaga, Kevina Etoru Anyumel
pmc-12579448.description: Hemosuccus pancreaticus (HP) is a rare cause of upper gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding, characterized by bleeding into the GI tract via the pancreatic duct and major papilla. It often occurs in conjunction with chronic pancreatitis and the development of pseudoaneurysms in the vessels near the pancreas.

pmc-12630503.title: Exploring the evolving role of apolipoproteins in oncology: global trends and emerging frontiers
pmc-12630503.creator: Dianzhe Tian, Zixuan Hu, Zuyi Yang, Lvyuxing Zhao, Haitao Zhao, Xinting Sang, Shunda Du, Yunping Luo, Lei Zhang, Yiyao Xu, Xin Lu
pmc-12630503.description: BackgroundMetabolic reprogramming, especially lipid metabolism, is crucial in cancer progression and treatment resistance. Apolipoproteins are crucial targets for research as they regulate autophagy, oxidative stress, and chemoresistance. A systematic bibliometric and bioinformatics approach is necessary to identify trends and elucidate the molecular mechanisms linking apolipoproteins to cancer.

pmc-12664825.title: Large‐Scale Passive Acoustic Monitoring Data Shows Seasonal and Diel Diversity in Foraging Behaviour of Harbour Porpoises Within Their Distributional Range in the Northeast Atlantic
pmc-12664825.creator: Jasmine Stavenow Jerremalm, Julie Beesau, Julia Carlström, Pia Eriksson, Mark Jessopp, Ailbhe Kavanagh, Olli Loisa, Mathilde Michel, Kylie Owen, Marianne Helene Rasmussen, Flore Samaran, Nicole Rose Eileen Todd, Emer Rogan
pmc-12664825.description: Latitudinal gradient can influence ecosystem dynamics and species distribution, yet the influence on some aspects, such as intra‐species diversity, is less well understood. The large‐scale distribution of harbour porpoises ( Phocoena phocoena ) in the Northeast Atlantic, indicates that ecological adaptations within the species might be greater than currently recognised.

pmc-12967050.title: Clinical Features, Mechanisms, and Management of Anxiety in Youth with Tic Disorders: A Narrative Review
pmc-12967050.creator: Si Zhang, Fei Han, Jie Chen, Xiaohua Shen, Yan Li
pmc-12967050.description: Tourette syndrome (TS) and related tic disorders (TD) are neurodevelopmental conditions primarily characterized by motor and vocal tics. However, coexistent anxiety has emerged as a pivotal yet under-recognized clinical determinant, at times overshadowing core tic symptomatology. This review delineates distinct anxiety phenotypes in youth with TD that differ from primary anxiety disorders.

pmc-13301985.title: Real-Life Orthokeratology for Myopia Control in Hungarian Children: A Five-Year Study of Axial Length Changes
pmc-13301985.creator: Beáta Tapasztó, János Németh, Illés Kovács, Zoltán Zsolt Nagy
pmc-13301985.description: Purpose: Orthokeratology is an established intervention for myopia control, but long-term European real-world data remain limited. This study evaluated 5-year axial length (AL) progression in Hungarian children undergoing orthokeratology and explored predictors of treatment response. Methods: This retrospective longitudinal study included 100 myopic children (198 eyes) treated with orthokeratology and followed for 5 years.

pmc-13547365.creator: Zhulin Wang, Qian Li
